Atom 11 on ligand 1 is the azine carbon bearing the trifluoromethyl at atom 12, so I can swap the C4 group with the cyclopentyl cap fixed - which means this episode cannot win on Phi, since that cap holds QED near 0.82. So I will spend it on the one question the scan has not answered. Electronics are clearly not what C4 reads: trifluoromethyl and methylamino both hit 0.61 from opposite ends, and the spread among withdrawing groups alone runs 0.51 to 0.61. What every good group has in common is being bigger than a methyl or a fluorine. But I have no idea where that stops - the largest things I have tried are iodine and a trifluoromethyl, both compact. A phenyl is a large step up: planar, extended, entirely carbon, and roughly twice the volume of a bromine. If it holds 0.60 or better then aryl substituents at C4 are a new direction worth pairing with a light cap next generation; if it collapses, I have found the ceiling on size and the position is a small, defined pocket.
